subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should extension-relay CDP clients adopt nonce-scoped opaque public target IDs that stay stable only for one shared-tab binding and are retired on tab removal, tab-ID reuse, or relay restart?
rationale: This is a compatibility-sensitive public browser-control contract; source review can assess implementation consistency but cannot choose the permanent identity semantics or migration posture.

options.title: Approve opaque per-binding handles
options.body: Accept the nonce-scoped handle contract after live paired-extension proof verifies continuity and stale-handle retirement.

options.title: Retain raw IDs temporarily
options.body: Keep current raw target-ID behavior and land only the route-level no-inference changes until a migration-compatible relay contract is designed.

options.title: Define another compatibility contract
options.body: Specify a different public identity or transition policy before merging the relay-bridge portion of this PR.

recommendation.title: Approve opaque per-binding handles
recommendation.body: Accept the nonce-scoped handle contract after live paired-extension proof verifies continuity and stale-handle retirement.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report supplies the detailed identity lifecycle requirements and is the clearest available product-contract signal.
